walkthroughs.body_html:
Number & Algebra — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Number & Algebra brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Number & Algebra.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
(x + 3)^2 equals 2x + 6.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
(x + 3)^2 equals 2x + 6.
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
(x + 3)^2 equals 2x + 6.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
(x + 3)^2 equals x^2 + 9 because squaring distributes over addition.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prime number”?
options: Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cube number”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Irrational number”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Square number”?
options: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Integer”?
options: A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rational number”?
options: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
